extensions.themeNote: Paper is the default ground and is therefore canonical: the bare :root carries it, and every colorMeta entry gives its drafting-film counterpart under `film`. Four palettes exist and agree value for value: bare :root (paper), @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) scoped to :root:not([data-theme="light"]) (film), :root[data-theme="light"], :root[data-theme="dark"]. Each of the last two restates the full palette so the manual toggle wins in both directions. color-scheme is `light dark`.

paper.purpose: The sheet, and the fill of every control and field on it. --paper and --surface are the same value.

desk.purpose: The ground the sheet lies on, carrying a faint two-gradient fibre tooth at 1.2% black. Also the source colour of every scrim, each a color-mix of it.

paper-inset.purpose: Content nested inside something else: code bodies, the detail panel, the room log, board cards, the log tail, the palette input.

rule-heavy.purpose: The printed rule that outlines a control and tops a stratum. The heavier of the two border weights.

rule-hair.purpose: The hairline that divides a row, a section or a table line, including every dashed separator.

ink.purpose: Reading colour, and the depth number in the margin. Measures 12.66:1 on paper, 13.34:1 on film.

ink-faded.purpose: Every secondary string, and the ticks on the depth rule. Measures 6.18:1 on paper, 5.88:1 on film.

oxide.purpose: The pencil mark being made now: the live stratum's depth rule, the selected tab's tick, the streaming caret, tool lines, links, the focus ring, the primary fill, a claimed todo.

oxide-wash.purpose: Oxide at low alpha. The spinner's unlit track, the search-hit mark, and the 45-degree hatch of a model-only layer. Never a control fill.

on-oxide.purpose: Text on an oxide fill. Measures 4.52:1 on paper, 6.10:1 on film; the tightest pair in the system.

lichen.purpose: A gate that held: the held mark in a turn's foot, a tool node's border and bar, an enabled plugin, a closed todo, this instance's own messages, string tokens in code.

grease-red.purpose: A gate that did not hold: failure text, a failed node's 2px border, the 90-degree fail hatch, a high-priority or late card, a bad toast. Failure only, never a warning.

on-grease.purpose: Text on a grease-red fill. Measures 6.84:1 on paper, 5.91:1 on film. Same value as On Oxide in both renditions, kept as its own token.

ochre.purpose: A limit approaching, not yet crossed: a column over its WIP limit, a card due soon, an open dependency. Exists so red never has to mean warning.

extensions.contrastNote: Measured against every ground each role renders on. Paper: ink 12.66:1, ink-faded 6.18:1, lichen 4.92:1, grease-red 5.87:1, on-oxide over oxide 4.52:1. Film: nothing below 4.97:1. Two paper-rendition pairs fall under 4.5:1 and are only AA at large or bold sizes: oxide as text on paper 3.88:1 (the 22px bold wordmark clears the 3:1 large-text threshold; a 16px link does not) and ochre as text on paper 4.16:1. New body-size text takes ink or ink-faded.

wordmark.purpose: The clanker title block in the header, in oxide. The only mono heading in the system.

heading.purpose: Every section heading, and h3 in rendered markdown. Text face, not mono: a heading is prose.

depth.purpose: The stratum's index, right-aligned in the margin against the rule. The signature type role.

body.purpose: The task as written, the answer, primary button labels, textareas, markdown paragraphs. Capped at --measure (70ch).

data.purpose: The dominant role: metrics, timestamps, code, tables, node labels, room messages, tool names, selects, JSON trees, the log tail.

caps.purpose: Column and panel headings inside a section, uppercase and tracked 0.06em to 0.08em. Weight 700 when it names a thing, 400 when it merely heads a column.

label.purpose: The printed label above a field, on its own row. The one uppercase role in the text face.

meta.purpose: The lithology legend, .meta readings, the held mark. The smallest size in the system.

typographyMeta.scaleNote: Five steps are defined (--step--1 0.6875rem, --step-0 0.8125rem, --step-1 1rem, --step-2 1.375rem, --step-3 1.875rem). --step-3 is unused. Body line-height is 1.55 throughout; code and the log tail drop to 1.5, headings to 1.2, the depth number to 1.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The sheet on the desk. One use in the system, on main. Offset and blur, never a zero-offset halo.

shadows.name: lift-high
shadows.purpose: Defined and currently unused. Reserved for a second sheet lifted off the first, not for hover emphasis.

shadows.name: float-scrim
shadows.purpose: Toasts and the jump-to-latest control: layers over the page rather than on the desk.

shadows.name: rail-scrim
shadows.purpose: The rail once it becomes a fixed panel below 60rem.

shadows.name: inset-mark
shadows.purpose: Selection on a palette row and the current board card. Dropped under forced-colors, where Highlight/HighlightText take over.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: Tool-running spinner, a 2px oxide-wash ring with an oxide top. Under reduced motion the ring is hidden and the word it stood for is shown.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: The ellipsis on an answer awaiting its first token. Under reduced motion it settles to opacity 0.6.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: A 0.6ch oxide block marking a live stream. Under reduced motion it settles to opacity 0.6.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: A toast entering on a 0.4rem translateY. Removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button :active feedback. Suppressed under reduced motion.

motion.name: disclosure
motion.purpose: The chevron mask rotating 90 degrees on an open details. Suppressed under reduced motion.

motion.name: rail-slide
motion.purpose: The narrow-screen rail panel. Suppressed under reduced motion.

motion.name: skip-reveal
motion.purpose: Both skip links travelling from off-screen to top: 0.75rem on focus. Suppressed under reduced motion.

motion.name: scroll-behavior
motion.purpose: JS-initiated scrollIntoView. Chosen at call time from matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'), since a CSS media query cannot reach a scrollIntoView argument.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Header and sheet padding drop to 1rem, definition lists collapse to one column, toolbar buttons go full width, tool params become one column.

breakpoints.name: rail
breakpoints.purpose: The rail leaves the flow and becomes a fixed min(20rem, 85vw) panel over a desk scrim, opened by the header Menu chip and hidden from the tab order when closed.

container.purpose: A lifted paper sheet with rule-heavy left and right borders and min-height 100vh, beside a sticky rail. Views are tab panels; exactly one is visible at a time.

hatching.tool: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg-muted) 22%, transparent) 0 1px, transparent 1px 6px)
hatching.fail: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--danger) 30%, transparent) 0 2px, transparent 2px 5px)
hatching.purpose: A stratum's kind is drawn, not merely coloured, so the distinction survives greyscale, colour blindness and forced-colors. The key is printed once above the transcript.

icons.aria: aria-hidden="true" focusable="false": each icon sits inside a control that already carries its accessible name.
placed: chevron (as a CSS mask on details markers)

extensions.forcedColors: Under forced-colors: active every box that relied on a border takes 1px solid ButtonText (buttons, chips, textarea, select, .turn, run nodes, iter tags, code blocks, copy buttons), graph edges take CanvasText, :focus-visible takes Highlight, and the four inset-shadow selection states (rail tab, rail item, palette item, board card) take Highlight/HighlightText with forced-color-adjust: none.

narrative.overview:
The surface is a field log sheet. A machine editing itself lays down strata; the owner reads the column and decides which layers hold. Turns are not chat bubbles and not cards: each one is a stratum bedded into a sheet of paper, numbered in the margin against a ruled depth column, banded by what the layer is made of. The composer sits at the foot of the column, where the next layer lands.

The scene decided the ground. This page is read beside a terminal in a lit room, on paper the owner annotates, so paper (#e8e2d6) is the default rendition and drafting film (#221d18) is the night one. That is the reverse of the category habit, and it was chosen deliberately: the rejected world is the dark agent console with a neon accent and a chat column, and its opposite, the pastel friendly-AI page.

Colour carries one job each and no job twice. Oxide orange is the active mark: the layer being deposited, the current section, a link, focus. Lichen green is a gate that held. Grease-pencil red is one that did not. A separate ochre carries a limit approaching, so red never has to mean "warning". Everything else is ink on paper. Prose is set in the system text face; every measurement is set in mono with tabular numerals, because a logged quantity has to line up in a column.
keyCharacteristics: Paper by default, drafting film at night; four palettes that agree value for value
A ruled depth column down the sheet, each turn a numbered stratum
Lithology hatching so kind survives greyscale, colour blindness and forced-colors
One accent, spent only on the active mark
Mono for measurements, the text face for prose; the choice of face is a claim about the content
Square corners (2-3px); round only where the thing is physically round
Drawn icons on one 24 grid at stroke 1.75; no glyph stands in for an icon

rules.name: The One Mark Rule
rules.body: Oxide means the thing being deposited now. If two elements on a screen are oxide, one of them is not the active mark.

rules.name: The Gate Rule
rules.body: Lichen means a gate held, grease red means it did not, ochre means a limit is approaching. Red is never a warning and never emphasis.

rules.name: The Two Rules Rule
rules.body: rule-heavy outlines what you can touch and tops a stratum; rule-hair divides rows and sections. Using the heavy rule for a passive divider makes the sheet look interactive where it is not.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every text role was measured against every ground it renders on, in both renditions. Paper: ink 12.66:1, ink faded 6.18:1, lichen 4.92:1, grease red 5.87:1, on-oxide over oxide 4.52:1 (the tightest fill pair in the system). Film: nothing below 4.97:1. Two paper-rendition pairs sit under 4.5:1 and are therefore only AA at large or bold sizes: oxide as text on paper (3.88:1, which the 22px bold wordmark clears at the 3:1 large-text threshold but a 16px link does not) and ochre as text on paper (4.16:1). Do not extend either use; new body-size text takes ink or ink faded.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: A logged quantity is mono and tabular; prose is the text face. Choosing the face is choosing what the content is, so a number that lands in the text face is a bug in the markup, not a style preference.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: --step--1 (0.6875rem) is the smallest size in the system. Anything that wants to be smaller gets ink faded instead.

rules.name: The Depth Column Rule
rules.body: Every stratum is measured against the ruled spine at --gutter. Only the index and the lithology band live in that margin. Content starts at the gutter, never inside it.

rules.name: The One Sheet Rule
rules.body: The sheet is lifted; everything on it is printed. A new surface that wants a shadow is asking to be a second sheet, and usually should be a ruled section instead.

rules.name: The Cut Sheet Rule
rules.body: Square corners by default. If a new element wants a radius above 3px, it has to be round, and it has to be small.

rules.name: The Drawn Not Coloured Rule
rules.body: A distinction that matters is drawn as well as coloured. Hatching survives greyscale, colour blindness and forced-colors; a fill alone does not.

rules.name: The Drawn Icon Rule
rules.body: No glyph stands in for an icon. A new icon is a path on the 24 grid at stroke 1.75, or it does not ship.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Every animation has a reduced-motion alternative that keeps the state change legible, not one that freezes it. The tool spinner is hidden and the word it stood for is shown; the streaming caret and the pending ellipsis settle to opacity 0.6; the toast, the press, the rail slide, the disclosure rotation and the skip-link travel are removed; JS-initiated scrolling reads matchMedia and passes auto.

rules.name: The Focus Ring Rule
rules.body: :focus-visible is a 2px oxide outline at 2px offset, declared globally and never removed, and Highlight under forced-colors. Every action reachable by pointer is reachable and visible by keyboard.

rules.name: The Forced Colors Rule
rules.body: Under forced-colors: active every box that relied on a border gets 1px solid ButtonText, graph edges take CanvasText, and the four selection states that are carried by an inset shadow (rail tab, rail item, palette item, board card) take Highlight / HighlightText with forced-color-adjust: none, because forced-colors drops box-shadow.

dos: Do spend oxide on the active mark only: the live layer, the current section, focus, a link, the one primary action.
Do use lichen for a gate that held, grease red for one that did not, and ochre for a limit approaching. Red means failure, never warning.
Do set measurements in mono with tabular numerals and prose in the text face; the face is the claim about what the content is.
Do measure a new turn-like thing against the depth column at --gutter and number it in the margin.
Do draw a distinction as well as colour it, and print the key once.
Do keep corners square (2-3px), reserving the pill for things that are physically round.
Do cap prose at --measure (70ch) and let anything wider scroll inside its own box.
Do give every animation a reduced-motion alternative that keeps the state change legible.
Do hold interactive targets at 44px, dropping to 32px only for a control that repeats down a list.
Do state absence plainly: "No turns in this conversation yet.", "(nothing recorded for this node)", "did not hold".
donts: Don't treat the dark rendition as the default. Paper is the ground; film is the night reading of the same sheet, and both are complete palettes.
Don't add a second accent, or spend oxide twice on one screen.
Don't use grease red for emphasis or for a warning; ochre exists for the approaching limit.
Don't lift anything else. The sheet carries the only --lift in the system, and --lift-high is not a hover treatment.
Don't set body-size text in oxide or ochre on the paper rendition; they measure 3.88:1 and 4.16:1 there.
Don't put a glyph, emoji or dingbat where an icon belongs, or draw an icon at another stroke weight.
